title: Power Automate desktop flows: encrypt and decrypt files with PGP
summary: Hold: the briefing calls licensing unpublished even though Microsoft's desktop-automation licensing rules cover these actions, and it overlooks applicable flow-run billing. The PowerShell example never prepares the connector objects it submits, and the summary promises PGP data-policy coverage that the body correctly says is unconfirmed.

The desktop-flows reference documents a PGP Cryptography action group for file encryption and decryption using OpenPGP.
claims.quote: The PGP Cryptography group of actions provides a set of tools for encrypting and decrypting files by using the OpenPGP (PGP) standard.

claims.claim: Encrypt file with PGP encrypts a file with the recipient's public key.
claims.quote: By using these actions, you can protect sensitive files by encrypting them with a recipient's public key.

claims.claim: The public key can be supplied as a file path or ASCII-armored text.
claims.quote: Whether you provide the public key as a file path or as ASCII-armored text.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: Decrypt file with PGP uses the corresponding private key and passphrase to decrypt PGP-encrypted files.
claims.quote: You can also decrypt PGP-encrypted files by using the corresponding private key and passphrase.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance

claims.quote: Use these actions to securely exchange files with external systems, business partners, and applications that support PGP encryption.

claims.claim: The maker can select ASCII armor for encrypted output.
claims.quote: Wraps the encrypted output in ASCII armor (text format starting with -----BEGIN PGP MESSAGE-----).

claims.claim: ASCII armor is disabled by default.
claims.quote: | ASCII armor | No | Boolean | False | Wraps the encrypted output in ASCII armor

claims.claim: Encrypted output is raw binary when ASCII armor is disabled.
claims.quote: When disabled, the output is raw binary data.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Open questions
claims.claim: The PGP documentation does not confirm automatic sensitive treatment of private-key and passphrase inputs.
claims.quote: Searched: "PGP" "sensitive" "Power Automate" passphrase; Power Automate PGP Cryptography DLP module tenant disable switch sensitive passphrase automatically. Opened PGP actions, Manage variables and Secure your data; no PGP-specific automatic masking statement found.

claims.claim: The passphrase field accepts Direct encrypted input or a text value.
claims.quote: | Passphrase | Yes | Direct encrypted input or Text value |

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Direct inputs use the local machine's DPAPI and cannot be decrypted when the flow runs on another machine.
claims.quote: The error occurs because direct inputs are encrypted using the local machine's Data Protection API (DPAPI) and can't be decrypted when the flow is run on another machine.

claims.claim: A wrong or outdated public key produces a file the partner cannot decrypt.
claims.quote: Searched: "PGP" "Invalid PGP key" recipient expired. Opened PGP Cryptography actions. It requires the corresponding private key, but does not state that an outdated key necessarily prevents a partner from decrypting.
claims.fix: Replace 'A wrong or outdated key produces a file the partner cannot decrypt' with advice: 'Verify the partner's public key before encryption.'

claims.claim: Invalid PGP key covers unparseable keys but not keys belonging to a different recipient.
claims.quote: Searched: "PGP" "Invalid PGP key" recipient expired. Opened both PGP action exception tables; they say the key 'isn't valid or couldn't be parsed' and do not define recipient-validation behavior.
claims.fix: Replace the clause with: 'Microsoft describes the Invalid PGP key exception as indicating that the specified key is not valid or could not be parsed.'

claims.claim: The reference lists encryption failure, key-file-not-found, invalid-key and incorrect-passphrase exceptions.
claims.quote: Failed to encrypt file with PGP; Key file not found; Invalid PGP key; Incorrect passphrase

claims.claim: The visibility setting is at Power Platform admin center > Settings > Tenant settings > Desktop flow actions in DLP > Show desktop flow actions in DLP policies.
claims.quote: On the left side panel, select Settings. On the Tenant settings page, select Desktop flow actions in DLP. Turn on Show desktop flow actions in DLP policies, and then select Save.

claims.claim: The printed Get-DesktopFlowModules and Add-ConnectorsToPolicy sequence supplies desktop-flow modules to the policy's Blocked group.
claims.quote: # Step #3: Convert the list of Power Automate for desktop flow modules to a format that can be added to the policy
claims.fix: The sequence assigns $modules but passes an uninitialized $modulesToAdd, omitting the documented connector-object conversion. Replace both printed copies with: $modules = Get-DesktopFlowModules; $modulesToAdd = @(); foreach ($module in $modules) { $modulesToAdd += [pscustomobject]@{ id = $module.id; name = $module.Properties.displayName; type = $module.type } }; Add-ConnectorsToPolicy -Connectors $modulesToAdd -PolicyName '<policy GUID>' -Classification Blocked. Keep the existing docs URL, whose complete example prepares these id/name/type objects before the call.

claims.claim: A maker marks a variable sensitive by right-clicking it in the variables pane and selecting Mark as sensitive.
claims.quote: To mark a variable as sensitive, right-click it in the variables pane and select Mark as sensitive.

claims.claim: No API or PowerShell operation for the maker's Mark as sensitive control is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Automate desktop flow mark variable sensitive API PowerShell; "desktop flow" "sensitive" "API" mark variable. Opened Manage variables and Secure your data; results document designer controls, not an API for this setting.

claims.claim: General desktop-flow DLP policies classify modules and individual module actions as Business, Non-business or Blocked.
claims.quote: Power Automate allows you to create and enforce DLP policies that classify desktop flow modules and individual module actions as Business, Non-business, or Blocked.

claims.claim: Admins can govern the PGP actions through data policies.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Automate PGP Cryptography DLP module tenant disable switch sensitive passphrase automatically. Opened PGP Cryptography actions and prevent-data-loss; neither identifies PGP's DLP module or expressly confirms coverage, as the body itself acknowledges.
claims.fix: Replace the summary's 'admins can govern them through data policies' with 'admins should review general desktop-flow data policies, whose PGP module mapping Microsoft has not confirmed'. Retain the qualified general-control row and its existing note.

claims.claim: The Show desktop flow actions in DLP policies visibility setting is tenant-scoped.
claims.quote: You need to turn on the Show desktop flow actions in DLP policies setting in your tenant settings.

claims.claim: Desktop-flow modules not explicitly classified in a policy group are not blocked even when the default group is Blocked.
claims.quote: Desktop flow modules that aren't explicitly added to any group aren't subject to the default group classification and aren't blocked, even if the default group is set to Blocked.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: After rollout

claims.quote: When desktop flow modules are added to DLP policies, your tenant's desktop flows are evaluated against them, and they're suspended if they're noncompliant.

claims.quote: Searched: Power Automate PGP Cryptography DLP module tenant disable switch sensitive passphrase automatically. Read the complete Desktop flow modules in DLP list on prevent-data-loss; Cryptography is listed, PGP is not.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model and notes; Cost and licensing; Open questions; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Licensing for these desktop-flow actions is unpublished, so the licensing model is unknown.
claims.quote: With a Power Automate Premium user license, users gain the full set of capabilities for cloud and desktop automation
claims.fix: Set licensing.model to 'included'. Replace the broad unpublished-licensing statements, including the cost rationale and the first Open questions bullet, with: 'Power Automate Premium includes the full set of desktop automation capabilities. For unattended desktop flows, Microsoft documents Power Automate Process licensing or pay-as-you-go. The PGP reference does not state a separate PGP licence.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/power-automate-licensing/types. Retain the narrow observation that the PGP action page itself lists no licence; do not infer unpublished platform licensing from that omission.

claims.claim: No Copilot Credit or other usage meter is documented for running these actions.
claims.quote: Desktop flow runs in a pay-as-you-go environment are charged as follows:
claims.fix: Replace the blanket no-meter sentence with: 'The PGP action reference lists no PGP-specific usage meter. Desktop-flow runs can be billed under the Power Automate flow runs (preview) meter when pay-as-you-go applies.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/pay-as-you-go-meters. Qualify 'The costs the sources show are indirect' as 'Incremental implementation costs include maker time, admin time and key management; existing desktop-flow licensing and applicable flow-run billing still apply.' A low rating can describe incremental implementation work, not an exemption from platform billing.

claims.claim: The PGP action-reference page itself specifies no role for using the actions.
claims.quote: Searched: "Power Automate" "PGP" role prerequisites license. Read the complete PGP Cryptography actions reference; it names no administrator or maker security role.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The PGP action-reference page itself specifies no meter.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Automate PGP actions licensing license premium pricing credits meter. Read the complete PGP Cryptography actions reference; no meter, credit rate or billing unit appears there. Platform flow-run billing is documented separately.
